lines.text: Why is this cell folded? Because the road ahead is narrower than the cell.
lines.phonemes: wˌaɪ ɪz ðɪs sˈɛl fˈəʊldɪd? bɪkˈɒz ðə ɹˈəʊd ɐhˈɛd ɪz nˈaɹəʊə ðɐn ðə sˈɛl.

lines.text: Meet a red blood cell: a disc about seven micrometers across, dimpled on both sides, with no nucleus. You have about twenty-five trillion of them: most of your own cells.
lines.phonemes: mˈiːt ɐ ɹˈɛd blˈʌd sˈɛl: ɐ dˈɪsk ɐbˌaʊt sˈɛvən mˈaɪkɹəʊmˌiːtəz əkɹˈɒs, dˈɪmpəld ˌɒn bˈəʊθ sˈaɪdz, wɪð nˈəʊ njˈuːkliəs . juː hav ɐbˌaʊt twˈɛntifˈaɪv tɹˈɪliən ɒv ðˌɛm: mˈəʊst əv jɔːɹ ˈəʊn sˈɛlz.

lines.text: Now follow it as the vessel branches, and branches again, into a capillary. The narrowest are slimmer than the cell, so cells go through in single file.
lines.phonemes: nˈaʊ fˈɒləʊ ɪt az ðə vˈɛsəl bɹˈantʃɪz, and bɹˈantʃɪz ɐɡˈɛn, ˌɪntʊ ɐ kəpˈɪləɹi . ðə nˈaɹəʊɪst ɑː slˈɪmə ðɐn ðə sˈɛl, sˌəʊ sˈɛlz ɡˌəʊ θɹuː ɪn sˈɪŋɡəl fˈaɪl.

lines.text: Here's the trick. The dimples give it spare surface for its volume, so it can fold into a parachute without stretching. Squeeze, slide, spring back.
lines.phonemes: hˈiəz ðə tɹˈɪk. ðə dˈɪmpəlz ɡˈɪv ɪt spˈeə sˈɜːfɪs fɔːɹ ɪts vˈɒljuːm, sˌəʊ ɪt kan fˈəʊld ˌɪntʊ ɐ pˈaɹəʃˌuːt wɪðˌaʊt stɹˈɛtʃɪŋ. skwˈiːz, slˈaɪd, spɹˈɪŋ bˈak.

lines.text: The tightest are about three micrometers: less than half its width. And it squeezes through them for its whole life: about a hundred and twenty days.
lines.phonemes: ðə tˈaɪtɪst ɑːɹ ɐbˌaʊt θɹˈiː mˈaɪkɹəʊmˌiːtəz : lˈɛs ðɐn hˈɑːf ɪts wˈɪtθ. and ɪt skwˈiːzɪz θɹuː ðˌɛm fɔːɹ ɪts hˈəʊl lˈaɪf: ɐbˌaʊt ɐ hˈʌndɹɪd and twˈɛnti dˈeɪz.

lines.text: So that dimple isn't decoration. It gets your blood through your smallest vessels, where oxygen is handed out.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ ðat dˈɪmpəl ˌɪzənt dˌɛkəɹˈeɪʃən. ɪt ɡˈɛts jɔː blˈʌd θɹuː jɔː smˈɔːlɪst vˈɛsəlz, wˌeəɹ ˈɒksɪdʒən ɪz hˈandɪd ˈaʊt.

lines.text: Meanwhile, as you watched, your bone marrow made over a hundred million new red cells.
lines.phonemes: mˈiːnwaɪl, az juː wˈɒtʃt, jɔː bˈəʊn mˈaɹəʊ mˌeɪd ˌəʊvəɹ ɐ hˈʌndɹɪd mˈɪliən njˈuː ɹˈɛd sˈɛlz.

lines.text: Next time: what this cell is carrying. About a billion passengers.
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst tˈaɪm: wˌɒt ðɪs sˈɛl ɪz kˈaɹiɪŋ. ɐbˌaʊt ɐ bˈɪliən pˈasɪndʒəz.
